title: Building a Smarter AI Agent with Neural RAG - Will Bryk, Exa.ai
talk_summary: Will Bryk argues search engines built for humans are mismatched to AI agents, which can issue long semantic queries, consume many results, and need controllable filters. Exa exposes neural and keyword search in one API and demos an agent composing semantic discovery with exact keyword lookups.

takeaways.technique: Hybrid search tool with explicit modes
takeaways.what_they_do: Exa exposes neural and keyword search as toggles in one API; the agent chooses the mode per query.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have like neural and keyword search. So you could try different ones.

takeaways.what_they_do: The demo agent first does a neural search to get a list of people, extracts names, then keyword-searches each name for GitHub info.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent will make uh a neural search to get a list of people extract the names and then search those using a keyword search

takeaways.what_they_do: Exa argues AI agents should search with multi-paragraph context, not short human keyword queries.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need a search engine that could literally handle multiple paragraphs of text

takeaways.what_they_do: The search API exposes result count, date ranges, domain filters, and other toggles because the AI caller needs control.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want the toggles because your AI is actually going to be calling this

takeaways.what_they_do: Exa lets AI request 10, 100, or 1,000 results because AI can process more than a human top-10 list.
takeaways.evidence_quote: number of results, 10, 100, a thousand, whatever it is
